---
title: "Get started"
description: "Run the same analysis with a local model bundle, Hugging Face weights, or the hosted River API."
---

## Run a first analysis

Give River a weekly history of spend, controls such as price, and an outcome such as sales. Give it a second table for the weeks you want to forecast. The [River-1 quickstart notebook](examples/river_1_quickstart.ipynb) makes both tables from synthetic data and runs this example:

```python
import pymc_mfm as mfm

roles = {
    "date_column": "week",
    "target_column": "sales",
    "channel_columns": ["tv", "search"],
    "control_columns": ["price"],
}
model = mfm.load("models/my-model", **roles)
result = model.inference(history, future, n_samples=100, random_seed=0)

result.plot.inputs()
result.plot.fit()
result.plot.contributions_over_time()
result.plot.shares()
```

The charts show the inputs, expected versus observed sales, weekly contributions, and each channel's or control's share of expected sales. `result.idata` holds the history (`context`) and forecast (`query`) draws in an `xarray.DataTree`. `model.plot` also draws from the latest result. The example uses 100 draws for a quick look; the default is 1,000.

## Choose where River runs

Change only the `mfm.load(...)` call in the notebook. Inference, results, and charts are the same Python calls for every source.

### Use a local bundle or Hugging Face {#decompose-a-time-series}

The example loads a bundle you already have. Replace `"models/my-model"` with the path to your bundle directory. For the pinned River-1 bundle on Hugging Face, use:

```python
model = mfm.load("river-1", **roles)
```

The River-1 weights are not public. The alias downloads the pinned bundle from the private PyMC Labs Hugging Face collection. If you have access, use `hf auth login`, set `HF_TOKEN`, or pass a Hugging Face `token=`. A local folder needs no credentials. See [Load and share models](models-hub.qmd) for other repositories and profiles.

### Use the hosted River API {#hosted-api}

```python
model = mfm.load("river-1", engine="hosted", **roles)
```

Inference sends the history and plan to the service and retrieves the results. It does not download model weights or need PyTorch. Use the synthetic data unless your invitation allows your own.

#### Get access

Access is by invitation. Set `MFM_API_URL` to the service URL and `MFM_API_KEY` to the personal key from the console's **Connect** page. You can pass `token=` instead of setting `MFM_API_KEY`; keep the key out of notebooks and shared files. This key is separate from Hugging Face authentication. See the [River API access instructions](http-api.qmd#get-access) for details.

## Install {#install}

::: {#install-client}
:::

::: {#use-the-python-library}
:::

PyMC MFM needs **Python 3.13 or newer**. Install it with any of:

```bash
pip install pymc-mfm
uv add pymc-mfm                         # in a uv project; or uv pip install pymc-mfm
conda install -c conda-forge pymc-mfm   # or: pixi add pymc-mfm
```

The one package covers every source in this guide: local bundles, Hugging Face loading, the hosted River client, per-draw files and plots. There are no extras. Hosted analysis does not import PyTorch or download weights, but PyTorch is part of the install.

On Linux, pip and uv install the CUDA build of PyTorch, about 3 GB of downloads. On a machine without a GPU, install the CPU build first with `pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu`, or configure uv as in [Using uv with PyTorch](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/pytorch/). On an Intel Mac, install from conda-forge: PyPI has no PyTorch wheels for it. In a uv project, set `requires-python = ">=3.13"` in its `pyproject.toml`, because uv resolves for every Python version the project allows.

If you installed `pymc-mfm` 0.1.2, a client-only build published by mistake, run `pip uninstall pymc-mfm` first; in a uv project, run `uv remove pymc-mfm`, then `uv add pymc-mfm`.

## Use your own data

Use one row per week, oldest first, with no gaps. Include the outcome in `history`. In `future`, include the same date, channel and control columns starting exactly one week after the history ends. See [input limits for hosted analysis](http-api.qmd#use-your-own-data) before you upload anything.

River is pretrained, so inference does not fit a model on your data. Its intervals describe uncertainty in the expected outcome, exclude observation noise, and are not evidence of causal lift. Read the [River-1 limits](../models/river-1/index.qmd#limits) before using results in a decision.
